s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdomen with chronic symptoms and weight loss, complicated by prior bariatric surgery
salient_findings: Right lower abdominal pain
Nausea and vomiting with bile
Localized tenderness and rebound pain in the right lower abdomen
Free gas under the right diaphragm on plain abdominal radiography
Thickened intestinal wall on abdominal CT
key_facts: 56-year-old male
Right lower abdominal pain for one month
Nausea and vomiting for one month
Vomitus includes stomach contents and bile
History of bariatric surgery 10 years prior
Weight loss of 23 kg due to poor appetite and abdominal pain
Localized tenderness and rebound pain in the right lower abdomen
Active bowel sounds
Sound of gas passing through water
Stable vital signs
Elevated white blood cells and neutrophils
Elevated C-reactive protein
Low albumin
Normal renal function and coagulation tests
Free gas under the right diaphragm on plain abdominal radiography
Dilated upper jejunum with 'spring sign' on plain abdominal radiography
Scattered pneumatosis in abdominal cavity on abdominal CT
Thickened intestinal wall on abdominal CT
Dense tubular shadows in narrow lumen on abdominal CT

shortlist.label: Intestinal obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of bariatric surgery, weight loss, and symptoms of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, with imaging showing dilated upper jejunum and scattered pneumatosis

shortlist.label: Internal hernia
shortlist.why_kept: History of bariatric surgery increases risk of internal hernia, and patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Adhesional bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of bariatric surgery and abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting are consistent with adhesional bowel obstruction, and imaging shows dilated upper jejunum

shortlist.label: Perforated peptic ulcer
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has free gas under the right diaphragm on plain abdominal radiography and elevated white blood cells and C-reactive protein, which are consistent with a perforated peptic ulcer

shortlist.label: Roux-en-Y syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of bariatric surgery and symptoms of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, with imaging showing dilated upper jejunum and scattered pneumatosis, which are consistent with Roux-en-Y syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's history of bariatric surgery, symptoms of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, along with imaging findings of dilated upper jejunum with 'spring sign' and scattered pneumatosis in the abdominal cavity, are consistent with an internal hernia, a known complication of bariatric surgery.

rejected.label: Intestinal obstruction
rejected.why: While the patient has symptoms and imaging findings consistent with obstruction, the specific findings and history point more towards an internal hernia as the cause of the obstruction.

rejected.label: Adhesional bowel obstruction
rejected.why: There is no clear history of previous abdominal surgery or other causes of adhesions that would lead to this diagnosis, making internal hernia a more likely cause given the patient's bariatric surgery history.

rejected.label: Perforated peptic ulcer
rejected.why: The presence of free gas under the diaphragm could suggest a perforation, but the overall clinical and imaging picture, including the 'spring sign' and the patient's history, is more indicative of an internal hernia.

rejected.label: Roux-en-Y syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is a possible complication of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery, but the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more specifically suggestive of an internal hernia rather than the broader category of Roux-en-Y syndrome complications.
